 Prelim Results | Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit
 Live Results, Highlights, Post-Fight Interviews With The Prelim Winners And More From Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit, Live From Madison Square Garden On November 14, 2026 
 By E. Spencer Kyte, On X: @SpencerKyte
 • Nov. 15, 2026
 The Polymarket UFC 334 prelims at Madison Square Garden served as an excellent opening act to Saturday’s loaded main card, delivering an entertaining mix of decisions and finishes with impact.
 Watch On Paramount+ (US) | How To Watch In Your Country 
 From veterans Evan Elder and Cesar Almeida teaching a couple younger fighters lessons to Bia Mesquita and Terrance McKinney claiming impressive first-round finishes, there was a little bit of everything on the way to the final two bouts on the slate, where Chris Duncan and Drew Dober established the Fight of the Night measure for the evening before Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson closed out the prelims — and his career — in spectacular fashion.
 If you missed any of the action, get caught up with our recaps below.
 Polymarket UFC 334 Prelim Results 
 More Coverage: Main Card Results | Official Scorecards 
 Stephen Thompson defeated Charles Radtke by TKO (spinning wheel kick) at 2:54 of Round 3 
 Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson closed out his career with one last win on the big stage, building into the fight and stopping Charles Radtke by third-round knockout.
 Radtke did well to close the distance and lean on his wrestling in the opening round, neutralizing Thompson’s advantage in the striking department. But as the fight progressed, “Wonderboy” found his range and started to punish Radtke, whose gas tank was running empty. After nearly finishing at the end of the second, Thompson connected with a spinning wheel kick in center of the Octagon midway through the third, dropping and finishing Radtke to close things out in spectacular fashion.

 Highlight reel debut, highlight reel finish — it just feels right. What a beautiful performance from the 43-year-old, who goes down as one of the most entertaining welterweights of all time and a true class act.
 Chris Duncan defeated Drew Dober by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) 
 Chris Duncan and Drew Dober teamed up to set the Fight of the Night bar towards the end of the prelims, getting into the back-and-forth battle on the feet most anticipated when the bout was announced.
 Duncan was the more effective of the two in the opening round, taking advantage of his length to largely keep Dober from getting inside and landing anything significant in response. While the American was able to close the gap in the second, Duncan still appeared to land the better blows before Dober was the sharper and fresher of the two in the final stanza, hurting Duncan in the late stages to make things a little more interesting when the horn sounded.
 When the scorecards were totaled, it was Duncan that came out ahead, earning a quick return to the win column after landing on the wrong side of things in his first main event last time out. “The Problem” is a staple in the 11-20 range in the lightweight division, and should remain so for the foreseeable future, turning in battles like this each time out.
 Terrance McKinney defeated Jim Miller by KO (strikes) at 1:53 of Round 1 
 Terrance McKinney capped his days in the lightweight division with a first-round stoppage win over Jim Miller.

 This was the ninth straight contest where McKinney’s fight ended in five minutes or less, and a reminder of the danger that is present every time he steps into the Octagon. After a bad weight miss on Friday, McKinney said he’s moving to welterweight, and it will be interesting to see how he does making the move up the divisional ladder in 2027.
 Cesar Almeida defeated Donte Johnson by TKO (strikes) at 3:20 of Round 1 
 Cesar Almeida bounced Donte Johnson from the ranks of the unbeaten on Saturday, getting the better of things in a middleweight firefight to open the televised prelims.

 The two men, who had trained together in the past, spent the entirety of the contest trading blows on the feet without any real feeling out process. Neither landed anything too spicy in the opening half of the round, but once Almeida got his timing down, he started to piece up Johnson, eventually rocking, wobbling, and finishing the previously undefeated prospect.

 This was an emotional win for Almeida, who fought back tears throughout his post-fight interview, snapping a two-fight slide with the victory. A decorated kickboxer, his technique and experience ruled the day on Saturday, and should continue to make him a dangerous threat just beyond the Top 15.
 Melquizael Costa defeated Jared Gordon by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 
 Melquizael Costa gutted out a good win over Jared Gordon in his return to the lightweight division on Saturday, getting the better of the striking in the first and third to garner the win on the scorecards.

 Costa, who was climbing the featherweight ranks earlier this year, got off to a great start, peppering Gordon with strikes from range and dictating the action on the feet. Gordon was able to close the distance and utilize his grappling for much of the second and early in the third, but failed to do much damage, with Costa working back to his feet and once again finding success in the striking down the stretch of the third.
 The judges were called upon to determine the victor and when their scorecards were collected and tallied, it was Costa that came out ahead, registering a win in his return to the 155-pound weight class. It’ll be interesting to see how far Costa can climb in the deepest division of the sport, but this was surely a good start and a step in the right direction.
 Bia Mesquita defeated Macy Chiasson by submission (rear-naked choke) at 3:23 of Round 1 
 Bia Mesquita continued her dominant march forward in the women’s bantamweight division, earning a first-round submission win over Macy Chiasson to earn her fourth consecutive UFC win.

 That’s now four wins and four finishes inside the Octagon for “The Lady GOAT,” who remains unbeaten and takes another big step forward in the division. She became the first woman to earn four straight submission wins in the UFC and passed former champ Ronda Rousey for the most submission wins in women’s bantamweight division history.
 Juan Diaz defeated Alatengheili by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27) 
 Juan Diaz picked up the second win of his rookie year in the UFC on Saturday, out-working Chinese veteran Alatengheili on the feet to collect a unanimous decision win.

 /

 The Dana White's Contender Series, Season 9 alum was the sharper and more efficient of the two from the outset, landing at a quality clip and doing well to limit the damage coming back his way. While he couldn’t find a finishing blow or get to a point where he had “The Mongolian Knight” in a real bad way, Alantengheili hasn’t been finished since his pre-UFC days, and Diaz was in complete control from start to finish in this one.
 If not for Diaz missing weight on Friday (he was 0.4 pounds over the 136-pound limit), this would have been a perfect outing for “Pegajoso,” who extended his winning streak to 10 with the win. The 28-year-old has clear and obvious upside, so the key will be securing the right matchups and making the right tactical choices inside the Octagon in order to keep stacking wins and moving forward in the division.
 Evan Elder defeated Samuel Sanches by unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 30-26) 
 More than 18 months on the sidelines didn’t slow Evan Elder’s momentum as the American lightweight returned to the Octagon and pushed his winning streak to four, spoiling the promotional debut of Dana White’s Contender Series grad Samuel Sanches.

 Elder took the fight to the Brazilian newcomer straight away, hurting Sanches in their initial exchange while looking to mix in takedown attempts against the lanky newcomer. As the fight progressed, Sanches had some moments of his own, only for Elder to frequently respond by landing something sharp or changing levels and shifting the location of the fight.
 All three judges scored the fight in favor of Elder, who advanced to 4-2 inside the Octagon and 11-2 overall with the win. It’s never been a question of talent for Elder, and if he can stay healthy and active, he has a chance to climb the ranks and continue having success.
